items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: Why can't you play with it. Why can't you play with it. Why can't you play with Levi? Well, I don't like that. You don't like it. I don't like that. I don't like that. I've got no interest.

ctx.x: And that was both my studies. Do you remember any special Rhodes that you liked?

Well, we had so many of them. Some of them, you know, because I just had, just learn the trombone. Some of them I could play, some of them I couldn't play. So I just had to play the ones that I knew I was really waiting on them until, for them to like this get to play. that done, then I tried something else. I would never give up. That's the way I had my trombone. It's like it is now. I go in any place, got a music box playing that. But they ain't playing that up to the top. What the music called? They ain't…

Well, I've been noticing lately. I don't want to mention any names. But there's a famous trumpet player from here. And I heard him playing with an old-time clarinet player. The trumpet player got off the melody and the clarinet player comes right in on it. To hold the melody down.
